editorial:
Ever wonder what happens when a marriage starts with a giant prank? You get a wild ride in this old-school comedy where a husband decides the only way to handle his flighty, unpredictable wife is to give her a real scare. He pretends to be a burglar, breaking into his own home to teach her a lesson about safety and stability. It is a lighthearted, quirky setup that feels like a chaotic game of cat and mouse, making you root for the husband while laughing at how out of control the situation gets.

The acting is surprisingly snappy for a film from 1927, and the pacing keeps you interested even without modern effects. While some of the jokes feel a bit dated, the physical comedy still lands well. If you enjoy vintage films with a mischievous twist, you will love this one. Since it is a rare find, you should look for a high-quality restoration. I suggest adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture, or check if you can rent it on Apple TV to see those crisp black-and-white details in your own living room.
endingExplained: The prank eventually goes too far, leading to a big confrontation where the truth comes out. After the chaos settles, the wife realizes that her husband's weird plan actually came from a place of love and a desire to keep her grounded. They both laugh off the madness and decide to start their marriage over with more honesty. It ends on a sweet note with the couple finally finding some common ground and peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old silent-era comedies and funny relationship drama.
